## Algebraic structures

<a id="Counts"></a>

### Counts

`Counts` · `src/algebra.ts:19` · status: **held**

The natural numbers that count things: the elements of a list, the characters of a run, levels and layers. Whether a collection is empty, has a single element or several is a question about its count.

The operations are written in `./code/algebra/counts.ts`.

| Law | Checked |
|---|---|
| A collection is empty, single or several: exactly one of the three | held on 100 draws |
| Any is the opposite of isEmpty, for a list, a text and a set | held on 100 draws |
| Zero counts nothing; the next count after zero counts one element | held on 100 draws |
| Previous undoes next, and next undoes previous | held on 100 draws |
| Between counts the integers from lo to hi, both included | held on 100 draws |
| Tally counts each element once, under its key, in the order where the keys first appear | held on 100 draws |
| The largest of nothing is zero; the largest of two lists put together is the larger of their two largest | held on 100 draws |

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `zero` | `0` | The count of nothing: no element, no change. The identity of addition |
| `one` | `1` | A single element; what a count grows by when one more thing is counted |

<a id="Sequences"></a>

### Sequences

`Sequences` · `src/algebra.ts:91` · status: **held**

Positions in a list or in a text: the first, the last, the one before, what follows. Positions start where ECMAScript starts them, and follow one another by one. A position where there is nothing gives nothing.

The operations are written in `./code/algebra/sequences.ts`.

| Law | Checked |
|---|---|
| Head and rest take a sequence apart: x first, then what follows | held on 100 draws |
| An empty sequence, or no sequence at all, has no head and no last element | held on 100 draws |
| The last element of a sequence that ends with x is x, at the only last position | held on 100 draws |
| The last n elements end the sequence, in its order: all of them when there are fewer | held on 100 draws |
| The head is at the only first position | held on 100 draws |
| Previous gives the element just before a position, and nothing before the first | held on 100 draws |
| What take keeps, followed by the rest, is the whole sequence | held on 100 draws |
| Pairs gives every two elements once, each pair in their order | held on 100 draws |
| Position finds where x first is, and nothing when x is not there | held on 100 draws |
| RemoveAt takes the element at a position out of the list, and gives it back | held on 100 draws |
| AtOrLast gives the element at a position, or the last one beyond the end | held on 100 draws |
| Times calls f once per count, with the positions in order from the first | held on 100 draws |

<a id="Texts"></a>

### Texts

`Texts` · `src/algebra.ts:201` · status: **held**

The monoid of texts: concatenation puts them one after the other, and the empty text changes nothing. It is what shows when there is nothing to show: an absent value folds into it.

The operations are written in `./code/algebra/texts.ts`.

| Law | Checked |
|---|---|
| The empty text changes nothing in a concatenation, and is the concatenation of nothing | held on 100 draws |
| Concatenation is associative | held on 100 draws |
| Optional keeps what is there, and shows nothing for undefined or null | held on 100 draws |
| When shows only what holds: false, zero, the empty text and absence do not | held on 100 draws |
| Without removes a part where it first appears | held on 100 draws |
| Lower words puts the joint where a camel-case name changes word, and writes it in lower case | held on 100 draws |
| Squeeze leaves the words, one space between each, and no white space at either end | held on 100 draws |
| Shorten leaves a text that is not too long as it is; a longer one keeps its beginning, then the ellipsis | held on 100 draws |

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `empty` | `""` | The text with no characters: the identity of concatenation, what nothing shows |
| `space` | `" "` | What separates words (U+0020, space) |
| `ellipsis` | `…` | Marks where a text was cut short (U+2026, horizontal ellipsis), or what is left out of it |
| `wordBoundary` | `(\p{Ll}\|\p{Nd})(\p{Lu})` | Where a name written in camel case changes word: a lower-case letter or a digit, then a capital |
| `everyWord` | `gu` | Every change of word, read in Unicode |

<a id="ValueTypes"></a>

### Types of values

`ValueTypes` · `src/algebra.ts:285` · status: **held**

What a value is, as ECMAScript's typeof tells it, said by name: a text, a number, a boolean, a function, a symbol, an object (null is not one, whatever typeof says). A body that asks says isText, not the word typeof gives.

The operations are written in `./code/algebra/values.ts`.

| Law | Checked |
|---|---|
| A value has at most one of these types; null, undefined and a big integer have none | held on 100 draws |
| Each kind of value is told by its own test: a list is an object, a function is not | held on 100 draws |
